claims.text: A machine-learning model trained on high-entropy-alloy crystal structures and thermal-conductivity values can accurately identify alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The machine-learning approach will outperform current predictions by at least 15%.
The target materials are solid, polycrystalline high-entropy alloys.
The model is trained on at least 1000 samples.
Crystal structures are represented by atomic coordinates and lattice parameters.
Atomic arrangement in the crystal lattice affects phonon scattering.
Atomic arrangement in the crystal lattice affects thermal conductivity.
The model can learn structural patterns that correlate with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Increased lattice disorder is associated with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Increased phonon scattering is associated with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The approach will predict phonon thermal conductivity values at least 15% lower than current predictions.
The model will achieve an RMSE below 0.05 W/m-K.
The comparison baseline consists of predictions from molecular-dynamics simulations or empirical models.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys containing no more than five principal elements.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys having a mixing entropy of at least 1.5R.
Prediction accuracy may be limited by training-dataset quality and size.
Prediction accuracy may be limited by the selected machine-learning algorithm and hyperparameters.
The experimental benchmark uses 20 high-entropy alloys predicted to have low phonon thermal conductivity.
An RMSE greater than 0.1 W/m-K falsifies the hypothesis.
An average prediction-to-measurement difference greater than 20% falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis defines improvement as at least 15% better predictive performance, whereas the predicted outcome operationalizes it as conductivity predictions that are at least 15% lower. A lower predicted value is not necessarily a more accurate prediction.

The claimed RMSE target is below 0.05 W/m-K, but the stated rule falsifies the hypothesis only above 0.1 W/m-K. Results from 0.05 through 0.1 W/m-K would violate the claimed outcome without meeting the stated falsification rule.
